answer: A reputation-weighted staking bond resists Sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, and its weight grows only with verified completed work, not with the number of identities it spawns. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues slowly, while a ferrous anchor of locked funds makes mass fake identities expensive. A delta check then compares each newcomer behavior against established peers, slashing deposits when coordinated fakery appears, so attackers pay more than they can gain.
